content.text:
**Why the phone couldn't be reached.** Three checks block it, all deliberate:
- The relay lets a phone into the rooms of its own account's Macs only, or of a Mac shared with its team.
- Since 31 October, a phone accepts device commands only from Macs on its own account.
- A Mac lists only its owner's devices.

Being in the same Ripul room doesn't get past any of these.

**What I'd build:** a "Share my phone with this chat" option, built the same way as "Share my browser":
- The phone's owner turns it on from a card. The calls go over the chat's own connection, and only the chat owner's turns can use it.
- It stops when they press Stop, when the app closes, or after an hour. A banner on the phone shows while it's on, and every call leaves a line in the chat.
- Each tool says whether it reads, writes or deletes. Only reading tools are shared unless the owner allows more, and the phone itself does the checking.
- `theme_server` would be split into a read tool and an edit tool, because some of its actions delete the draft.
- It would be in developer builds only. Android gets almost all of it for free, because the check sits in the shared web page.

I wouldn't build a standing grant of a phone to a person: it would undo the 31 October fix.

The open questions are on a card.

file.content:
# Support sessions

Lets your app's customer show the app to somebody helping them, and lets that person point at
things in it. The customer signs in to nothing and installs nothing. It uses public Apple API
only, so it is the same in a store build as in a development build.

## What happens

1. The customer chooses **Get Help** in your app. The app asks Ripul for a six-digit code and
   shows it.
2. The customer reads the code to the supporter (on the phone, in a chat).
3. The supporter opens Ripul on an iPhone or Mac, goes to **Devices ▸ Help a Customer**, and
   enters the code.
4. Your app tells the customer who that is ("Helen Helper would like to see Shop") and what
   they will be able to do. Nothing is shared until the customer taps **Allow**.
5. The supporter sees your app, and only your app. A finger on their picture draws a ring on
   the customer's screen: "tap here". They can't tap, type or change anything; the customer
   does that.
6. A pill at the top of the customer's screen says who is watching, with **Stop**, for as long
   as the session runs.

## Adding it

SwiftUI:

```swift
import RipulAgent

struct HelpScreen: View {
    @State private var gettingHelp = false

    var body: some View {
        Button("Get Help") { gettingHelp = true }
            .ripulSupportSheet(isPresented: $gettingHelp,
                               configuration: RipulSupportConfiguration(siteKey: "pk_live_…"))
    }
}
```

UIKit:

```swift
RipulSupport.shared.present(from: self, configuration: RipulSupportConfiguration(siteKey: "pk_live_…"))
```

`RipulSupportConfiguration` takes the same publishable site key as `AgentConfiguration`. If your
app sends its own `Origin` on Ripul calls, pass it as `origin:`; it must be one the site key
allows. To build your own screen instead of `RipulSupportView`, observe `RipulSupport.shared.phase`
and call `start`, `allow` and `stop`.

## Who can use a code

The creator of the site key, and its owners and admins. To anyone else a real code and a wrong
one get the same answer, so a code can't be guessed at or probed for. A code that nobody takes
is forgotten after ten minutes; a session ends an hour after it is taken, or when either side
stops.

## What is and isn't shared

- The app's own window, as the app draws it. Not the keyboard, not the status bar, not other
  apps, not the home screen. Leaving the app pauses the picture; coming back carries on.
- Secure text fields are drawn as dots, as on screen.
- Nothing the supporter sends reaches the app. Their pointing is drawn in a window of its own
  over the app. Ripul's server enforces this as well: it passes the picture one way and
  pointing the other, and drops everything else.
- The picture travels over TLS through a room on Ripul's servers. It is not stored. It is not
  yet encrypted end to end between the two devices.

If a different supporter takes the code part-way through, the picture stops and the customer is
asked again.

## Limits today

- About five pictures a second while the screen moves and two at rest, at one pixel a point
  (text is readable, not sharp). The app draws its own window on the main thread to make each
  picture, which costs about 35–60 ms each, so scrolling in your app is a little less smooth
  while a session runs.
- One supporter at a time.
- iPhone and iPad apps. A Mac Catalyst app has not been tried.

## How it works

Both ends connect out to a room on Ripul's servers (`SupportRoom`, a Durable Object named by
the code), so neither needs to be on the same network as the other. The room carries Live
View's own stream (`LiveStreamWire`), one frame a WebSocket message. In the SDK the session is
`RipulSupport` (`Sources/RipulAgent/Support/`), which hands the room's channel to
`LiveStreamHost` in its support mode. The supporter's side is `SupportViewer.swift` in the
Ripul app.

To test without a second signed-in device, `ripul-native-app/support-probe` is a Mac
command-line supporter, and the Ripul app takes `-ripul.support.siteKey <key>` (be the
customer) and `-ripul.support.claim <base64>` (be the supporter) in debug builds.

entries.description:
Record something someone should act on later that will not be done in this turn, on the list this repository keeps for every chat and every Mac. Other agents read it with read_observations, and the user sees it in the chat's side panel and the repository's Observations list. Ripul stamps repository provenance from the selected checkout, and the chat and Mac.

Record one without being asked, in two cases:
- `tangent`: you noticed it while working on something else. A bug next door, a slow query in a log, a security smell, an enhancement worth making. Record it and carry on with your task; do not fix it unasked.
- `loose-end`: before you end a turn, if part of the task is not finished or not tidied up (a test you skipped, a workaround left in, a case not handled, a follow-up the user should know about), record it. Say what is missing, not what you did.

The test: would you tell a colleague about it before leaving? Style nits, things you will fix in this turn and the steps of this turn's work are not observations: those steps belong in your own todo list (TodoWrite). Anything that should outlive the turn is an observation.

`severity` is the harm if nobody acts: `critical` (data loss, a security hole, production down; it notifies the user's phone), `high` (a user-facing bug or a real slowdown), `medium` (worth doing soon), `low` (nice to have). Enhancements are usually low or medium.

Write `detail` in Markdown: the side panel and the repository's list render it as the chat renders a message. Give whoever picks it up what you know: what you saw, where, why it matters and what would fix it. Use what helps them read it: a short list of findings or steps, `code` for names, paths and commands, a fenced block for a log line, an error or a snippet, a link to an issue or a PR, a small table for measurements. The title stays one plain line.

Call with `title`, `severity` and `category` (and `detail`, `kind`, `files`) to record one. If open observations look like the same thing, nothing is recorded and they are listed: call … [truncated]

detail.description: What you saw, where, why it matters and what would fix it, in Markdown (lists, code spans and fenced blocks, links and tables are rendered). At most 4000 characters.

files.description: Up to 10 paths relative to the repository, each optionally with ":line", e.g. "src/api/list.ts:42".

force.description: Record or move it even though open observations in the destination look similar. Only when it really is a different thing.

id.description: An observation to move (with status) or amend (with new words), from this tool's list or read_observations.

moveToRepo.description: With id and note (why), move the observation to this absolute repository folder on the same Mac, keeping its attribution and history. Requires full access to both repositories; no content or status edits in the same call.

note.description: With seenAgain, one line on anything new; with moveToRepo, the required reason for moving.

repo.description: Absolute folder of the repository on this chat's Mac. Defaults to the chat folder. Member requests need full access for changes and read access for listing.

resolution.description: With status done or dropped, one line on how it was done or why it no longer applies.

seenAgain.description: The id of an open observation you saw again. Adds this chat's sighting instead of recording a new one.

status.description: With id. doing claims it for this chat; done and dropped need a resolution.

title.description: What is wrong or missing, in one line of at most 80 characters, e.g. "Session list query scans every row".

input.title: Phone sharing across accounts is designed and decided, not built
input.detail:
**Decided by Peter on 10 November 2026** (this chat's milestones), for letting one person's agent read another person's phone in an SDK app such as wac:

- **Two routes.** A *chat share* for team members with Ripul accounts, built like "Share my browser" (`memberBrowser.ts`), and *support sessions* for customers, who have no Ripul account (a code read out, then Allow, a pill with Stop; `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/support-sessions.md`).
- In **App Store builds too**.
- The phone answers **only while the app is open**.
- Reading the **screen needs its own consent**, separate from tools that read.
- Only the **chat owner's turns** may use it (on the support route, whoever took the code, in the chat they pick).

**Not built:**
1. An access field on `NativeTool` (iOS and Android): `read | write | destroys`, defaulting to `write`. Checked on the phone and by the server, never only on the asking Mac (its agent has a shell there).
2. wac: split `theme_server` into a read tool (`status`, `diff`, `local_diff`) and an edit tool. `discard_local`, `use_shipped`, `follow_server` and `publish_*` delete the phone's theme draft.
3. Chat route: `session.deviceOffer` / `deviceQuery` / `deviceResult` beside the browser offer, a banner with Stop on the phone, a line in the chat for every call. The 31 October guards (`servesDeviceToolsIn`, `isOwnersDevice`) stay as they are.
4. Support route: a tool-call frame kind in `SupportRoom.ts`'s `PASSED`, let through only for the tools ticked at Allow, and the supporter's Mac host joining as the supporter so an agent can call them.
5. Store builds: wac's Get Help is developer-only (`WAC/View Controller/ProfileVC/BetaFeaturesVC.swift:269-274`, wac repo). It needs to be visible and named in the App Review notes, and wac's privacy policy and App Store privacy label must say an AI assistant may read shifts and pay with consent. Developer tools stay compiled out, so `theme_server` still needs a developer build.
6. Android has no support sessions yet.

Suggested order: items 1 and 2 (both routes need them), then the chat route (unblocks reading a team member's draft theme), then the support route.

content.text:
Both routes, then: team members share a phone through the chat, and customers through support sessions. I've added that to the decision in the side panel.

Both routes need the same core pieces, so building the second costs much less than the first:
- tools marked as read-only, with the check made on the phone;
- separate ticks for the screen and for reading tools;
- a Stop button on the phone;
- a line in the chat for every call.

If it's built, I'd go in this order:
1. **Shared first:** the read-only marking and splitting `theme_server` into a read tool and an edit tool.
2. **The chat share next:** that's what makes Eden's draft theme readable.
3. **Support sessions last.**

Nothing has been built. The plan and your decisions are saved as a loose end in this repo's Observations, so whoever picks up the work starts from them.

---
name: project_support_sessions
description: "Support sessions: a customer of an SDK app shows the app to a signed-in supporter through a worker room, with a six-digit code; view and point only; verified between two simulators 3 Oct 2026; in WAC Beta (SDK 0.7.165, Beta Features > Help, not in the App Store build); builds published over the air, not yet tried on a real phone"
metadata:
  type: project
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
  scope_also: repo:wac-ios
---

3 October 2026: Peter asked for remote support for a consumer of the SDK, on main. He wanted Keyfall as the test app, but its repo is only on the other Mac (`~/Documents/repos/keyfall`, no remote), so he said "use WAC for now". Consumer doc: `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/support-sessions.md`.

What was built (b1f594692 … on main, worker deployed):

name: feedback_sdk_release_from_clean_worktree
description: "Publish an SDK tag from a detached worktree at HEAD when the monorepo SDK tree is dirty with another agent's WIP — never ALLOW_DIRTY=1, never stash"
metadata:
  type: feedback
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
---

`ripul-ios-sdk/scripts/release-public.sh` refuses a dirty `Sources`/`Package.swift`
tree because rsync copies the WORKING TREE, so another agent's in-flight edits ride
into the public tag (this already shipped an in-flight AgentScreen port as v0.4.14).
In this repo the SDK tree is dirty with foreign work most of the time.

**Do not** reach for `ALLOW_DIRTY=1`, and do not stash. Publish from a clean
detached worktree at the commit you actually want:

```bash
# 1. Stamp + commit the new version in MAIN first — the script's own stamp step
#    would commit to the worktree's detached HEAD and be lost.
sed -i '' 's/^let ripulSDKVersion = ".*"$/let ripulSDKVersion = "X.Y.Z"/' \
  ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/ViewInspectorOverlay.swift
git commit -m "chore(sdk): stamp ripulSDKVersion X.Y.Z" && git push

# 2. Release from a clean checkout of that commit.
git worktree add --detach /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z HEAD
cd /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z/ripul-ios-sdk && bash scripts/release-public.sh X.Y.Z --push
cd - && git worktree remove /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z --force   # ALWAYS remove it
```

Verify the tag got what you meant, in the public clone (`~/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk`):
`git show vX.Y.Z --name-only` lists your files, and `git show vX.Y.Z:<foreign file>`
fails.

**Why:** it gives the user their change on a public tag without touching, shipping,
or asking about another agent's uncommitted work — the only option that satisfies
both CLAUDE.md rule 4 (never silently work around a foreign dirty tree) and the
release script's concurrency guard. **How to apply:** any "release the SDK" /
"ship WAC against the new SDK" ask where `git status` shows SDK edits you did not
make. `/tmp` already holds ~35 stale ripul worktrees — remove yours when done.
See [[project_wac_ota_deploy_flow]], [[feedback_wac_ship_default_target]].

name: feedback_sdk_release_after_all_edits
description: Cut the ripul-ios-sdk tag only AFTER every SDK edit for the change is done — a late edit strands WAC on a tag without it
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback

  modified: 2026-07-28T08:39:43.264Z
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
  scope_also: repo:wac-ios
---

`release-public.sh vX.Y.Z --push` snapshots the SDK working tree at that moment. Any SDK
edit made *after* the tag — even one that builds clean locally — is NOT in the tag WAC
pins, so WAC fails with `cannot find type 'X' in scope` even though the symbol exists in
the monorepo.

Hit 2026-07-28: released 0.5.40, then made `RipulTokenNode`/`RipulTokenNodeScreen` public
so WAC's scope trees could share the builder. Local SDK build passed (it compiles the
monorepo copy); WAC's build failed against the 0.5.40 tag. Cost a full WAC rebuild cycle.

**Why:** the local `swift build`/`xcodebuild` of the SDK proves nothing about what WAC
sees — WAC resolves the PUBLIC repo at the pinned tag, a separate checkout.

**How to apply:** finish every SDK edit for the change (including access-level widening
discovered while wiring the host) → build SDK → *then* release + bump the pin. If a host
build fails on a missing SDK symbol, check `git log v<pinned>..HEAD -- ripul-ios-sdk/`
before debugging the host. See [[project_wac_consumes_sdk_as_pinned_public_package]].

name: feedback_sdk_behavioural_change_needs_pin_bump
description: A green host build only validates SDK changes that alter the API surface — behavioural SDK changes need the pin bumped BEFORE the check
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3a38c80e-bb09-43b5-98aa-662a86f4f64a
  modified: 2026-07-28T14:27:43.835Z
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
  scope_also: repo:wac-ios
---

When an SDK change is **behavioural** (rendering, layout, internal logic) rather than a new
or widened symbol, the host compiles fine against the OLD pinned tag. A green build then
proves nothing about the change, and the host ships without it while you report it done.

Hit twice on 2026-07-28:
- Singleton-kind *rendering* added in 0.5.48; WAC built green on 0.5.47 and would have
  shipped masthead as a library screen instead of a settings list.
- Singleton *preview* rendering added in 0.5.49; WAC built green on 0.5.48 and would have
  shipped the masthead screen with still no preview — the exact bug being fixed.

Both compiled because the host only calls pre-existing API (`register(kind:)`,
`supportsNamedStyles:`); the changed behaviour lives entirely inside the SDK.

**Why the earlier lesson doesn't cover it:** [[feedback_sdk_release_after_all_edits]] is
about a MISSING symbol, which the compiler catches loudly. This is the silent inverse.

**How to apply:** classify the SDK change first. New/widened symbol → a green host build is
meaningful. Behavioural only → release, bump the pin, and rebuild *before* claiming it
works, or verify on device. See [[project_wac_consumes_sdk_as_pinned_public_package]].

Never leave a memory in a fol

|---|---|---|---|---|

| WAC Android app | `~/Documents/repos/wac_android_final` | `v-2.6.2-location-tracking` | `02ff4a31` | 3 |

Those counts include the memories that sessions on each WAC repo had saved before, which had never been in git (about 80), and for the backend the five that were stranded under the repo's old path. Only the 66 that came from this store carry scope tags; the older ones are untagged.

**A live API token** was taken out of `project_wac_payslip_client_estimate.md` before it was committed to the WAC iPhone repo. The value is in ripul's history at `12e220979`.

**How to apply:** set `scope` (and `repo`) under `metadata` on every new memory. Save a memory about another codebase in that repo's tracked `.ripul/memories/` if it has one; otherwise save it here, tagged with its repo, and say so.

monorepo copy); WAC's build failed against the 0.5.40 tag. Cost a full WAC rebuild cycle.

**Why:** the local `swift build`/`xcodebuild` of the SDK proves nothing about what WAC
sees — WAC resolves the PUBLIC repo at the pinned tag, a separate checkout.

**How to apply:** finish every SDK edit for the change (including access-level widening
discovered while wiring the host) → build SDK → *then* release + bump the pin. If a host
build fails on a missing SDK symbol, check `git log v<pinned>..HEAD -- ripul-ios-sdk/`
before debugging the host. See [[project_wac_consumes_sdk_as_pinned_public_package]].

When an SDK change is **behavioural** (rendering, layout, internal logic) rather than a new
or widened symbol, the host compiles fine against the OLD pinned tag. A green build then
proves nothing about the change, and the host ships without it while you report it done.

Hit twice on 2026-07-28:
- Singleton-kind *rendering* added in 0.5.48; WAC built green on 0.5.47 and would have
  shipped masthead as a library screen instead of a settings list.
- Singleton *preview* rendering added in 0.5.49; WAC built green on 0.5.48 and would have
  shipped the masthead screen with still no preview — the exact bug being fixed.

Both compiled because the host only calls pre-existing API (`register(kind:)`,
`supportsNamedStyles:`); the changed behaviour lives entirely inside the SDK.

**Why the earlier lesson doesn't cover it:** [[feedback_sdk_release_after_all_edits]] is
about a MISSING symbol, which the compiler catches loudly. This is the silent inverse.

**How to apply:** classify the SDK change first. New/widened symbol → a green host build is
meaningful. Behavioural only → release, bump the pin, and rebuild *before* claiming it
works, or verify on device. See [[project_wac_consumes_sdk_as_pinned_public_package]].

# Claude

## Project Overview

This is a **web application** that provides AI-powered workflow automation and visualization capabilities.

### Architecture

| Component | Status | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| **Web Application** | Active | Primary codebase - React-based workflow platform |
| **Lightweight Extension** | Active | Minimal Chrome extension that augments the web app with browser-specific features |
| **Full Extension** | Legacy | Deprecated full Chrome extension - not actively maintained |

### Development Focus
- **DO**: Develop features in the web application
- **DO**: Keep the lightweight extension minimal (only browser API features)
- **DON'T**: Add new features to the legacy full extension
- **DON'T**: Frame this project as "a Chrome extension" - it's a web application

### Documentation

| Document | Contents |
|----------|----------|
| **[PROJECT-STRUCTURE.md](./docs/PROJECT-STRUCTURE.md)** | Cross-repo guide: chrome-extension, ripul-native-app, ripul-ios-sdk — structure, build commands, message protocol, and cross-repo dependencies |
| **[GLOSSARY.md](./GLOSSARY.md)** | Core domain terms (Tool, Prompt, PromptTool, MCP, etc.) |
| **[EXTENSION-ARCHITECTURE.md](./EXTENSION-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | Extension history, capabilities, and communication protocol |
| **[NATIVE-BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md](./docs/NATIVE-BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | Native iOS ↔ web communication: JS callables (preferred) vs message protocol (legacy) |
| **[DOM-MINIMIZATION-ARCHITECTURE.md](./docs/DOM-MINIMIZATION-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | DOM reduction pipeline, n-tagging strategy, and the semantic-minimization ↔ rehydration bridge |
| **[Tools System Architecture](./docs/architecture/toolsSystemArchitecture.md)** | End-to-end guide: tool definitions → interceptor chain → handler resolution → CLI bridge → native tools. Links to all subsystem docs |
| **[MCP Tool Surfaces](./docs/architecture/mcpToolSurfaces.md)** | Cross-package map of every MCP/tool surface — why each runtime context and surface exists, consumers, transports, name prefixes, and which gates are security vs curation. Start here for anything spanning CLI/native/device/extension tools |
| **[paneLatching.md](./docs/architecture/paneLatching.md)** | Three-pass plan for latching a mirror to an app's own UI element instead of a fixed crop — what each toolkit actually exposes, and why the manifest comes last |
| **[multiViewerMirroring.md](./docs/architecture/multiViewerMirroring.md)** | Multi-viewer window mirroring (implemented 2026-08-27): per-window captures with subscriber sets, one controller driving with loud refusal for the rest, shared crop, controller-only direct transport — plus the plan it grew from and the accepted gaps |
| **[webMcpAutoToolCreation.md](./docs/architecture/webMcpAutoToolCreation.md)** | How agent page interactions automatically become reusable WebMCP tools |
| **[databaseArchitecture.md](./docs/architecture/databaseArchitecture.md)** | D1 database layer: D1Store base class, scoping model, migrations, shared types, and data access patterns |
| **[rbacArchitecture.md](./docs/architecture/rbacArchitecture.md)** | RBAC enforcement: AuthContext flow, access guard policies, team authorization, handler categories |
| **[themingGuide.md](./docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md)** | Theme system: how to use MUI tokens, `alpha()`, `useThemeColors()`, and anti-patterns to avoid |
| **[iOS Styling Guide](../ripul-native-app/docs/ios-styling-guide.md)** | Native iOS glass effects: prefer `.clear` over `.regular`, vibrancy, and glass modifier library |

---

## Code Quality Rules

### After Code Changes
1. **Always run TypeScript compilation check** after making any code changes:
   ```bash
   npx tsgo --noEmit
   ```
2. Fix any TypeScript errors before considering the task complete
3. If there are build errors, investigate and resolve them immediately

### Testing
- Run relevant test commands if they exist
- Verify changes don't break existing functionality

---

## Technical Guidelines

### React Components
- Ensure proper TypeScript types for all components
- Check that all imports are correctly specified
- Verify that component props match their interfaces

### Workflow System
- The workflow graph uses React Flow for visualization
- Panels can appear in both chat log and workflow graph
- Messages with `.toolStatus` suffix appear in the workflow graph
- Base method names (without `.toolStatus`) create UI panels

### Styling
- Use Material-UI (MUI) components and styling system where possible
- Override styles with `!important` when necessary to override inline styles
- Consider both light and dark themes when making UI changes
- **Use MUI theme tokens** (`'text.primary'`, `'action.hover'`, `'divider'`) instead of hardcoded rgba values
- **Never pass string tokens to `alpha()`** — resolve via `theme.palette.X.main` first
- **Use `useThemeColors()` hook** for common color calculations instead of manual `alpha()` calls
- **Colours and typefaces come from the theme, never from a literal**: no hex or `rgba(` colour and no `fontFamily` string at a call site. Use a palette token, `alpha()` of a palette value, a named colour (`useNamedColours()`) or a family (`useFontFamilies()`). Mark a colour that is data `// theme-exempt: <reason>`
- **Run the literals check before pushing**: `node scripts/check-theme-literals.mjs --strict <paths>`. Every build runs it, and it fails the build for a literal in a finished directory (`src/logging/components/chat/`, `src/logging/panels/`)
- See [themingGuide.md](./docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md) for full details and anti-patterns

### Settings Panels
- For settings dialogs with toggles that reveal more options, follow the established patterns
- See [docs/features/ui/settingsPanelPatterns.md](docs/features/ui/settingsPanelPatterns.md)

### UI Element Traceability
- Add `data-ui` attribute to every rendered element in React components
- Format: `ComponentName.section.element` (e.g., `LLMRequestPanel.header.message`)
- Use static values only - never include runtime data (tool names, IDs, status values, etc.)
- Purpose: Enable tracing from DOM back to source code that created it
- Duplicates are acceptable when the same component is reused
- **MUI compound components** (`TextField`, `Autocomplete`, `Slider`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, etc.) render multiple DOM layers — `data-ui` on the component prop lands on the outer wrapper `div`, not the interactive `<input>`. For any MUI component wrapping a focusable element, also pass `data-ui` through `slotProps`:
  ```tsx
  // ❌ data-ui only reaches the wrapper div
  <TextField data-ui="Foo.bar" />

  // ✅ data-ui also reaches the <input>
  <TextField
    data-ui="Foo.bar"
    slotProps={{ htmlInput: { 'data-ui': 'Foo.bar' } }}
  />
  ```

---

## Deployment & Cloudflare Pages

### CRITICAL: `_routes.json`
- **Location:** `chrome-extension/_routes.json` (copied to `public/` during build)
- **Purpose:** Tells Cloudflare Pages which routes go through Functions vs static files
- `"include"` = routes handled by the Pages Function (`functions/api/[[path]].ts`)
- Everything NOT included is served as static files from `public/`
- **DO NOT** add broad patterns like `"include": ["/*"]` — this routes JS chunks through Functions, which returns `index.html` instead of JavaScript, breaking the entire app
- Current correct config: `/api/*`, the two `/.well-known/` app-link files, `/dl/*` (unlisted downloads from R2, `functions/dl/[[path]].ts`) and `/mac` with `/mac/*` (the address for installing the Mac apps, `functions/mac.ts` and `functions/mac/[product].ts`) — each a narrow path with its own Function. Also the iPhone install pages, each `<base>` with `<base>/*`: `/ios` with the two fixed manifests `/manifest.plist` and `/manifest-alice.plist` (Ripul, `functions/ios.ts`) and `/sandsend` (Sandsend Retreats, `functions/sandsend.ts`), both built on `functions/installPage.ts`

### Chunk Naming & CDN Caching
- Production builds name chunks `[name]-routed-[hash]` (content hash; set in `scripts/build.mjs`). The fixed namespace keeps them clear of the historical `chunk-HASH` URLs the March 2026 incident cached as HTML. A missing chunk answers a real 404 with `no-store`, so it cannot be cached
- The `_headers` file sets `/js/*` to `max-age=31536000, immutable` — if the CDN ever caches a wrong response for a chunk URL, it's stuck for a year unless the URL changes

### Each deployment keeps the last 20 builds' files live
- A page keeps running the build it loaded (a phone left open, the Mac host waiting for idle agents), and a Pages deployment serves only the files uploaded with it, so each deploy used to take away every chunk the new build renamed (0, 18 or 362 of ~707 per deploy, measured 30 October 2026)
- `build.mjs` writes `public/retained-builds.json` naming the new build's files. `scripts/retainBuilds.mjs`, run by `deploy:pages` and `deploy:sourcemaps` just before wrangler uploads, reads that file from the newest production deployment, keeps the newest 20 builds (fewer if the deployment would pass 15,000 files; the Free plan allows 20,000), copies their files into `public/js` and writes the manifest back. Pages uploads only files it does not already have
- The bytes come from `~/.ripul/web-build-cache` on the deploying Mac (exactly the kept builds' files) or from the deployment itself (each keeps its files at `https://<id>.ripul-app.pages.dev` for good). A deployment with no manifest has its build found by following imports from its pages
- It never stops a deploy: on any failure the new build ships alone, and the deploy log says `[retain-builds] FAILED`. The line `[retain-builds] kept N earlier builds…` says what each deploy carried. Tests: `node --test scripts/tests/retain-builds.test.mjs`

### Every lazy `import()` goes through one function
- `scripts/lazyImportRoute.mjs` rewrites each lazy `import("./x.js")` in the production bundle to `__rI__("./x.js")` (same length, so source maps hold), and each page that loads the bundle defines `__rI__` in its head. A failure reaches `handleLazyImportFailure` (`src/utils/lazyImport.ts`) whether or not the caller catches it: it reloads the page (onto the newer build after a deploy) and throws a `ChunkLoadError` worded for a person, or, when the site can't be reached, only the words. Before this, WebKit's "Importing a module script failed." reached cards and alerts from most of the ~800 lazy loads. With the last 20 builds kept live (above), it is the fallback for a page older than that
- WebKit and Chromium keep a module's failed load for the life of the page and never fetch it again, so retrying an `import()` is useless: only a reload brings the chunk back
- esbuild hashes a chunk **before** the rewrite, so a name must always mean the same rewrite: change `CHUNK_NAMESPACE` whenever the rewrite or `__rI__` changes, or a page on an older build can fetch new code calling a function its page never defined
- Tests: `node --test tests/lazy-import-route.browser.test.mjs` (WebKit and Chromium, a local production-style build) and `src/utils/lazyImport.test.ts`

### Incident Reference (2026-03-29)
Missing `_routes.json` in deploys caused Cloudflare to serve `index.html` for JS chunk requests. The immutable cache header then locked the wrong response into the CDN. Fixed by deploying `_routes.json` and adding build version to chunk names.

---

## Development Workflow

1. Understand the requirement
2. Investigate the codebase
3. Make the necessary changes
4. **Run `npx tsgo --noEmit` to check for TypeScript errors**
5. Fix any build errors
6. Test the functionality if possible
7. Document the changes made

---

## Common Commands

## Code Quality Rules

### After Code Changes
1. **Always run TypeScript compilation check** after making any code changes:
   ```bash
   npx tsgo --noEmit
   ```
2. Fix any TypeScript errors before considering the task complete
3. If there are build errors, investigate and resolve them immediately

### Testing
- Run relevant test commands if they exist
- Verify changes don't break existing functionality

---

## Technical Guidelines

### React Components
- Ensure proper TypeScript types for all components
- Check that all imports are correctly specified
- Verify that component props match their interfaces

### Workflow System
- The workflow graph uses React Flow for visualization
- Panels can appear in both chat log and workflow graph
- Messages with `.toolStatus` suffix appear in the workflow graph
- Base method names (without `.toolStatus`) create UI panels

### Styling
- Use Material-UI (MUI) components and styling system where possible
- Override styles with `!important` when necessary to override inline styles
- Consider both light and dark themes when making UI changes
- **Use MUI theme tokens** (`'text.primary'`, `'action.hover'`, `'divider'`) instead of hardcoded rgba values
- **Never pass string tokens to `alpha()`** — resolve via `theme.palette.X.main` first
- **Use `useThemeColors()` hook** for common color calculations instead of manual `alpha()` calls
- **Colours and typefaces come from the theme, never from a literal**: no hex or `rgba(` colour and no `fontFamily` string at a call site. Use a palette token, `alpha()` of a palette value, a named colour (`useNamedColours()`) or a family (`useFontFamilies()`). Mark a colour that is data `// theme-exempt: <reason>`
- **Run the literals check before pushing**: `node scripts/check-theme-literals.mjs --strict <paths>`. Every build runs it, and it fails the build for a literal in a finished directory (`src/logging/components/chat/`, `src/logging/panels/`)
- See [themingGuide.md](./docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md) for full details and anti-patterns

### Settings Panels
- For settings dialogs with toggles that reveal more options, follow the established patterns
- See [docs/features/ui/settingsPanelPatterns.md](docs/features/ui/settingsPanelPatterns.md)

### UI Element Traceability
- Add `data-ui` attribute to every rendered element in React components
- Format: `ComponentName.section.element` (e.g., `LLMRequestPanel.header.message`)
- Use static values only - never include runtime data (tool names, IDs, status values, etc.)
- Purpose: Enable tracing from DOM back to source code that created it
- Duplicates are acceptable when the same component is reused
- **MUI compound components** (`TextField`, `Autocomplete`, `Slider`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, etc.) render multiple DOM layers — `data-ui` on the component prop lands on the outer wrapper `div`, not the interactive `<input>`. For any MUI component wrapping a focusable element, also pass `data-ui` through `slotProps`:
  ```tsx
  // ❌ data-ui only reaches the wrapper div
  <TextField data-ui="Foo.bar" />

  // ✅ data-ui also reaches the <input>
  <TextField
    data-ui="Foo.bar"
    slotProps={{ htmlInput: { 'data-ui': 'Foo.bar' } }}
  />
  ```

## Deployment & Cloudflare Pages

### CRITICAL: `_routes.json`
- **Location:** `chrome-extension/_routes.json` (copied to `public/` during build)
- **Purpose:** Tells Cloudflare Pages which routes go through Functions vs static files
- `"include"` = routes handled by the Pages Function (`functions/api/[[path]].ts`)
- Everything NOT included is served as static files from `public/`
- **DO NOT** add broad patterns like `"include": ["/*"]` — this routes JS chunks through Functions, which returns `index.html` instead of JavaScript, breaking the entire app
- Current correct config: `/api/*`, the two `/.well-known/` app-link files, `/dl/*` (unlisted downloads from R2, `functions/dl/[[path]].ts`) and `/mac` with `/mac/*` (the address for installing the Mac apps, `functions/mac.ts` and `functions/mac/[product].ts`) — each a narrow path with its own Function. Also the iPhone install pages, each `<base>` with `<base>/*`: `/ios` with the two fixed manifests `/manifest.plist` and `/manifest-alice.plist` (Ripul, `functions/ios.ts`) and `/sandsend` (Sandsend Retreats, `functions/sandsend.ts`), both built on `functions/installPage.ts`

### Chunk Naming & CDN Caching
- Production builds name chunks `[name]-routed-[hash]` (content hash; set in `scripts/build.mjs`). The fixed namespace keeps them clear of the historical `chunk-HASH` URLs the March 2026 incident cached as HTML. A missing chunk answers a real 404 with `no-store`, so it cannot be cached
- The `_headers` file sets `/js/*` to `max-age=31536000, immutable` — if the CDN ever caches a wrong response for a chunk URL, it's stuck for a year unless the URL changes

### Each deployment keeps the last 20 builds' files live
- A page keeps running the build it loaded (a phone left open, the Mac host waiting for idle agents), and a Pages deployment serves only the files uploaded with it, so each deploy used to take away every chunk the new build renamed (0, 18 or 362 of ~707 per deploy, measured 30 October 2026)
- `build.mjs` writes `public/retained-builds.json` naming the new build's files. `scripts/retainBuilds.mjs`, run by `deploy:pages` and `deploy:sourcemaps` just before wrangler uploads, reads that file from the newest production deployment, keeps the newest 20 builds (fewer if the deployment would pass 15,000 files; the Free plan allows 20,000), copies their files into `public/js` and writes the manifest back. Pages uploads only files it does not already have
- The bytes come from `~/.ripul/web-build-cache` on the deploying Mac (exactly the kept builds' files) or from the deployment itself (each keeps its files at `https://<id>.ripul-app.pages.dev` for good). A deployment with no manifest has its build found by following imports from its pages
- It never stops a deploy: on any failure the new build ships alone, and the deploy log says `[retain-builds] FAILED`. The line `[retain-builds] kept N earlier builds…` says what each deploy carried. Tests: `node --test scripts/tests/retain-builds.test.mjs`

### Every lazy `import()` goes through one function
- `scripts/lazyImportRoute.mjs` rewrites each lazy `import("./x.js")` in the production bundle to `__rI__("./x.js")` (same length, so source maps hold), and each page that loads the bundle defines `__rI__` in its head. A failure reaches `handleLazyImportFailure` (`src/utils/lazyImport.ts`) whether or not the caller catches it: it reloads the page (onto the newer build after a deploy) and throws a `ChunkLoadError` worded for a person, or, when the site can't be reached, only the words. Before this, WebKit's "Importing a module script failed." reached cards and alerts from most of the ~800 lazy loads. With the last 20 builds kept live (above), it is the fallback for a page older than that
- WebKit and Chromium keep a module's failed load for the life of the page and never fetch it again, so retrying an `import()` is useless: only a reload brings the chunk back
- esbuild hashes a chunk **before** the rewrite, so a name must always mean the same rewrite: change `CHUNK_NAMESPACE` whenever the rewrite or `__rI__` changes, or a page on an older build can fetch new code calling a function its page never defined
- Tests: `node --test tests/lazy-import-route.browser.test.mjs` (WebKit and Chromium, a local production-style build) and `src/utils/lazyImport.test.ts`

### Incident Reference (2026-03-29)
Missing `_routes.json` in deploys caused Cloudflare to serve `index.html` for JS chunk requests. The immutable cache header then locked the wrong response into the CDN. Fixed by deploying `_routes.json` and adding build version to chunk names.

The cause: `DirectMacClient` (`ripul-native-app/iOS/DirectMacClient.swift`) stores paired Macs in the Keychain item `paired-hosts` (`DirectMacVault`, `Shared/DirectMacTransport.swift`). That item carries no Clerk user id and nothing clears it at sign-out. On the Mac, `DirectMacGrant` (`macOS/DirectMacHost.swift`) is likewise only a device id, name, secret and state. Direct trust is between a phone

**Why:** when testing with a second account on the same phone, a Direct Mac in New Chat is a leftover pairing on the device, not an account link.

**Clean baseline (since 2026-10-04, `3e226d649`, Alice 202610040526):** deleting the app does NOT clear this, because iOS keeps Keychain items after an app is deleted. Settings → Factory Reset on iPhone/iPad (`iOS/FactoryReset.swift`) now erases every Keychain item the app owns, the whole defaults domain (including the installation id, so the phone comes back as a new device), all web data stores 

**How to apply:** for a clean test, use Factory Reset, not app deletion. To remove one pairing, use Forget on the phone ("Pair or manage Macs") or Revoke under Paired Phones on the Mac. If accounts must be separated, tag each pairing with the Clerk user id at pair time (nil for standalone) and hide pairings that belong to another account. Related: [[Sandsend sees Peter's Mac chats through Test tea

name: Native builds from a git worktree
description: What a fresh worktree lacks before RipulApp builds (generated StandaloneRuntime, chrome-extension/node_modules for the bundled-interface script phase, xcodegen), plus how the SDK test bundle is run on a simulator
metadata:
  type: project
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
---

Learned 2026-09-20 building the chat-bubble feature in `.claude/worktrees/chat-bubble-expose-stop`.

**Why:** `xcodegen generate` fails on a fresh worktree because `ripul-native-app/StandaloneRuntime/` (gitignored output of `chrome-extension/scripts/build-standalone.mjs`) does not exist, and the RipulApp "Build bundled standalone interface" script phase then fails with `Cannot find package 'esbuild

**How to apply:**
- Copy the main checkout's generated bundle: `cp -R <main>/ripul-native-app/StandaloneRuntime/. <worktree>/ripul-native-app/StandaloneRuntime/` (or run the web build there).
- Symlink `ln -s <main>/chrome-extension/node_modules <worktree>/chrome-extension/node_modules`. **The symlink is NOT ignored** (checked 2026-09-27): a `node_modules/` rule matches only a directory, and a symlink is a file, so it shows as `?? chrome-extension/node_modules` and a broad `git add` woul
- Or skip the copy and run `node <worktree>/chrome-extension/scripts/build-standalone.mjs` once (after the symlink) — it generates StandaloneRuntime in ~3s.
- **A hand-run `xcodebuild` + `devicectl install` breaks Siri** (hit 2026-09-27):
  after the first build, `Metadata.appintents/` ships with only
  `extract.actionsdata` + `version.json` — no `root.ssu.yaml` — so every spoken
  App Shortcut phrase fails ("Siri can't control the Ripple app"). Deleting the
  directory and touching SiriAppIntents.swift does NOT bring it back on Xcode
  27.1. Use ship_ios.py's `repair_siri` recipe after every build: copy
  `build/Build/Intermediates.noindex/RipulNativeApp.build/Debug-iphoneos/RipulApp.build/ssu/root.ssu.yaml`
  into the app, then `codesign -d --extract-certificates=<prefix> <app>` (note
  the `=`: as a separate argument codesign takes the prefix as the target and
  fails — ship_ios.py passes it separately, so its device-mode repair likely
  fails the same way), `codesign --force --sign <sha1 of <prefix>0>
  --preserve-metadata=identifier,entitlements,flags,runtime
  --generate-entitlement-der <app>`, and `codesign --verify --deep --strict`.
  Never install without checking all three files are present.
- **Present is not enough — it can be STALE.** Incremental builds on Xcode 27.1
  don't regenerate the intermediate `root.ssu.yaml` either: after adding an App
  Shortcut, the file still listed only the old intents (generated hours
  earlier), so copying it in shipped a phrase model without the new shortcut.
  Check every non-schema intent in `extract.actionsdata` appears as
  `name: <Intent>_N` in the yaml; if not, build with `clean build` (only ~1 min
  more), which regenerates and copies it.
- Then `xcodegen generate` and build with the sanctioned `-derivedDataPath build` (relative to the worktree, so the first build is cold, ~4 min under Xcode 27).
- Use an Xcode 27 toolchain for the app and all harnesses so one DerivedData is not mixed between toolchains, and so the iOS 27 Siri schema intents (`#if compiler(>=6.4)`) are compiled in. As of 2026-09-27 the installed ones are `/Applications/Xcode.app` (26.4) and `/Applications/Xcode-27.1.app` — `

entries.name: EnterWorktree
entries.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

1	import Foundation
2	
3	// MARK: - NativeTool Protocol
4	//
5	// Conform to this protocol to expose any native API as a tool the agent can call.
6	//
7	// Naming convention:
8	//   pick_*      Interactive picker — presents native UI, waits for user selection.
9	//               Result is shown as a confirmation card in the agent chat.
10	//               Must return `name` (String) or `value` ([String: Any]) for display.
11	//   get_*/list_*  Read data — fetches info for the agent.
12	//   create_*/setup_*/delete_*  Write action — modifies app state.
13	//   run_*       Replays a developer-recorded workflow (a macro — see

{"guide":"# Working inside Ripul

You are a coding agent running inside Ripul Host, an app on the user's Mac. The user may be at the Mac, or driving this chat from an iPhone or another Mac, and other agents may be working on the same repository at the same time.

## Your process can end between turns

Process lifetime depends on the provider. Claude normally keeps one process per chat; changing its model or effort, switching accounts, rewinding, or reclaiming an idle chat can replace it. Codex normally uses a shared runtime, with model and effort applied to each turn: those choices do not imply a restart. Do not assume a child process will survive a host restart or runtime recovery. The saved conversation can resume even when the work its old process was running has ended.

So a job that takes more than a few minutes must not be a child of your process. Do not rely on a background task or a monitor for it. Run it as a job of Trainyard's:

```bash
ripul-train job --label "deploy staging" -- ./long-job.sh staging
```

Trainyard runs it in a session of its own, so it outlives your process, a Codex command's limits and a host restart, and keeps its log. The moment it ends, this chat is told its exit code, how long it ran and the end of its log, and that starts your next turn. So end your turn as soon as it has started: there is no time to guess and nothing to poll. Quote a pipeline as one argument (`-- 'make build && make test'`). `ripul-train jobs` lists the recent ones.

When this Mac is busy, a self-contained job (in a git checkout, naming nothing outside it) may run on another of the person's Macs with more room. Its log streams here, the files it changed come back when it ends, and the notice says where it ran. A file you change while it runs is kept, and the job's copy is put beside it as `<name>.from-<Mac>`. Add `--here` when a job needs this Mac as it is now, or `--anywhere` to send it to another Mac whenever one can take it.

Where Trainyard is not running, start it in a session of its own and read a log:

```bash
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import subprocess, sys; subprocess.Popen(["bash", "-c", sys.argv[1]], start_new_session=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=open(sys.argv[2], "a"), stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)' \
  'cd /path/to/project && ./long-job.sh; echo "EXIT_CODE=$?"' /tmp/long-job.log
tail -n 20 /tmp/long-job.log    # now, then on the turn a wake starts
```

`nohup … &` is not enough for every agent: Codex stops what a command started in the background once the command returns, `disown` included, and only a job in a new session outlives it. Change directory inside the detached command, and look at the first lines of the log straight away: a bad launch fails within a second. Then end your turn with a wake to read the log (see "Waiting without holding your turn"), rather than watching it in your turn or from a background loop.

## Waiting without holding your turn

Never wait inside your turn for something that takes more than a minute: a build, a train, a deploy, another agent, a timer. While a command waits, your turn stays open, and the person in the chat cannot talk to you, only interrupt you. Between 20 October and 3 November 2026, agents held turns open this way 935 times, for 125 hours in all.

Every such wait has a wake:

- **A train** you asked for tells this chat when it ends, and that starts your next turn (trains/deploy). Ask for it, say what you are waiting for, and end your turn.
- **Another agent's reply** comes back to this chat and starts a turn (session/agents).
- **A job** you started with `ripul-train job` (a deploy, a test run, a long build: anything that outlasts the turn) tells this chat when it ends, and that starts your next turn (see "Your process can end between turns").
- **Anything else**, such as a sweep at a set time or something outside this Mac: call `ripul_schedule` with `in` or `at` and a message saying what to read and what counts as done, then end your turn (session/later).

Do not reach for an `until … sleep` loop, chained sleeps, repeated `ripul-train status`, or a Monitor on a build or train. When Claude Code refuses a plain `sleep` and suggests an until-loop or Monitor, that advice is for a terminal, not for a Ripul chat. Waits that return within seconds, such as a simulator booting or a port opening, are fine. In a Claude chat Ripul adds a note to any command that waits a minute or more, and a train request run in your turn stops waiting once its train is held or queued, saying "End your turn: this chat is told when the train ends."

If another agent started you, ending your turn sends it your reply now. Say what is still running and what will wake you. When the wake comes, send the result with `send_to_agent`.

## Milestones

A long chat is hard for its user to follow, and the commits are too many and too fine to read. Record what the chat achieves as milestones, with the `milestone` tool, when the work reaches one and without being asked: the user sees them at the top of the chat's side panel, and each one jumps to its place in the conversation. The tool's description carries the rules for what counts as one.

## Ripul's tools

Ripul's tools come from the `ripul_tools` server. Their names say where they act: `host_…` on the Mac running Ripul Host, `device_…` on a connected phone, tablet or simulator, `browser_…` in Ripul's browser. Your client may list them by name only until you look one up.

## What agents learn about a repository

When a repository has a `.ripul/memories/` folder, that is where its agents' memories live, and it is tracked in git with the code. Save what you learn about the repository there, and commit it with the work.

## Finding the right instructions

`ripul_guide` with no arguments returns a short directory. A `topic` returns a suitability summary and its task sections; add `section` to read the chosen instructions before acting. You can go straight to a known section, or request `section: "all"` for the complete guide. These reads do not expand tool categories. Open a category only once its tools fit the task. Tool descriptions and parameter schemas carry each tool's detailed contract.

Keep useful links with `shortcut`, and record checked outcomes with `milestone`. Neither requires a separate user request.","next":"For another task, request this topic without section to see its section directory.","section":"start","title":"Start work","topic":"session"}

When Claude Code refuses a plain `sleep` and suggests an until-loop or Monitor, that advice is for a terminal, not for a Ripul chat. Waits that return within seconds, such as a simulator booting or a port opening, are fine. In a Claude chat Ripul adds a note to any command that waits a minute or more, and a train request run in your turn stops waiting once its train is held or queued, saying "End your turn: this chat is told when the train ends."

If another agent started you, ending your turn sends it your reply now. Say what is still running and what will wake you. When the wake comes, send the result with `send_to_agent`.

## Milestones

A long chat is hard for its user to follow, and the commits are too many and too fine to read. Record what the chat achieves as milestones, with the `milestone` tool, when the work reaches one and without being asked: the user sees them at the top of the chat's side panel, and each one jumps to its place in the conversation. The tool's description carries the rules for what counts as one.

## Ripul's tools

Ripul's tools come from the `ripul_tools` server. Their names say where they act: `host_…` on the Mac running Ripul Host, `device_…` on a connected phone, tablet or simulator, `browser_…` in Ripul's browser. Your client may list them by name only until you look one up.

## What agents learn about a repository

When a repository has a `.ripul/memories/` folder, that is where its agents' memories live, and it is tracked in git with the code. Save what you learn about the repository there, and commit it with the work.

## Finding the right instructions

`ripul_guide` with no arguments returns a short directory. A `topic` returns a suitability summary and its task sections; add `section` to read the chosen instructions before acting. You can go straight to a known section, or request `section: "all"` for the complete guide. These reads do not expand tool categories. Open a category only once its tools fit the task. Tool descriptions and parameter schemas carry each tool's detailed contract.

WAC consumes the RipulAgent SDK as a **remote pinned Swift package**, not a local
path (changed 2026-06-09 to fix dev-team build breaks). Three repos are involved:

- **Source of truth:** the `ripulio/ripul` monorepo, under `ripul-ios-sdk/`
  (locally `/Users/petermaude/Documents/repos/ripul/ripul-ios-sdk`).
- **Public release repo:** `github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk` (its own repo,
  locally `~/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk`). Was archived/read-only until 2026-06-09;
  now unarchived and active for periodic releases.
- **Consumer:** WAC `WAC.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` pins it via
  `XCRemoteSwiftPackageReference` → `https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk.git`
  at `kind = exactVersion; version = 0.2.0` (bumped from 0.1.0 on 2026-06-25).

**Current published version: v0.2.14** (commit `fceff3f` in the public repo).
(0.2.12 = single adaptive "Discuss in <chat>" explorer button; 0.2.13 = dedicated
element **Edit tab** — text + colour/alpha/corner/font/hidden live, intent
generalised to `edits:[Edit{property,from,to}]`; 0.2.14 = **resizable HUD** — drag
the panel's bottom-right corner; the UIKit move-pan yields that corner via
`gestureRecognizer(_:shouldReceive:)`.)
- v0.2.0 added `RipulViewExplorer` (host-agnostic launcher that mounts the native
  `ViewInspectorOverlay` over the app's key window — see [[view_explorer_shake]])
  plus accumulated monorepo SDK drift since v0.1.0 (AgentBridge/AgentView).
- v0.2.1 made the inspector reach non-interactive leaf views (it had landed only
  on interactive containers because `hitTest` skips `isUserInteractionEnabled ==
  false` views — the default for UILabel/UIImageView/most static UIKit content).
- v0.2.2 fixed that leaf-walk re-entering the inspector's OWN overlay: with the
  launcher, the overlay host is a sibling of app content under the top VC, so the
  walk kept landing on the full-screen `PassthroughRootView` HUD ("one big
  element"). `ViewInspectorController.isInspectorOwnView()` now excludes the
  overlay subtree (matches self, `PassthroughRootView`, and a tag —
  `ripulViewExplorerOverlayTag` — stamped on the launcher's host view).
- v0.2.3 fixed the probe selecting the system iOS 26 floating tab-bar host
  (`FloatingBarHostingView`) everywhere: the launcher's full-screen
  `UIHostingController` view (default user interaction) was swallowing the
  hitTest probe, so it never reached the app and the geometric fallback picked
  the frontmost full-screen view. `pickAt` now disables interaction on the whole
  tagged overlay root during the probe (via `inspectorOverlayRoot()`), so hitTest
  resolves through every passthrough layer to the real app view.
- v0.2.4 added a "Find in source" section to the inspector (UIKit views rarely
  set accessibilityIdentifier, so class alone wasn't enough to locate them):
  owning UIViewController (responder chain), visible text, UIControl
  target/action selectors, SF Symbol/asset name (parsed crash-safely from
  `UIImage.description`), restorationIdentifier, and a one-tap "Copy reference"
  that bundles them + the VC chain into a greppable block.
- v0.2.5 added the nearest app-defined ancestor class (`container`, e.g. the cell
  holding the element — `Bundle(for:) == .main`) and hardened the image-name
  parse (dropped the loose "name = " marker + `isPlausibleAssetName` validation)
  so description noise like "main:" is no longer shown.
- v0.2.6 added `propertyRef` ("Owner.property", e.g. `HomeVC.imgWeather`): resolves
  the @IBOutlet/stored property that holds the tapped view via Obj-C runtime
  reflection (scan app-bundle class layers of owning VCs/ancestor views for an
  object ivar whose value is the view). Zero annotation/build step, works in

5	// DEVELOPER tools for the theme pipeline and screen navigation — so theme state is read and
6	// changed through formal, inspectable operations instead of guessed from pixels or driven by
7	// blind taps. Registered `.developer` beside the functional-test tools (WACNativeTools).

9	private struct ThemeToolError: LocalizedError {
10	    let errorDescription: String?
11	    init(_ message: String) { errorDescription = message }
12	}
13	
14	/// Read every scene window, including overlays omitted by inspect_screen. A blank overlay
15	/// can cover WAC while its own window still reports Home. Do not load controllers' views,
16	/// capture pixels, or include user-facing text in this structural diagnostic.
17	@MainActor
18	enum WACWindowDiagnostics {
19	    static var snapshot: [String: Any] {
20	        let scenes = UIApplication.shared.connectedScenes.compactMap { $0 as? UIWindowScene }
21	        let root = appDelegate.window?.rootViewController
22	        return [
23	            "appRoot": root.map { controller($0) } ?? [:],
24	            "scenes": scenes.map { scene in
25	                ["activationState": scene.activationState.rawValue,
26	                 "windows": scene.windows.map { window in
27	                     ["class": String(describing: type(of: window)),
28	                      "isWACWindow": window === appDelegate.window,
29	                      "isKeyWindow": window.isKeyWindow,
30	                      "level": window.windowLevel.rawValue,
31	                      "hidden": window.isHidden,
32	                      "alpha": window.alpha,
33	                      "frame": NSCoder.string(for: window.frame),
34	                      "root": window.rootViewController.map { controller($0) } ?? [:],
35	                      "subviews": window.subviews.map { view($0) }] as [String: Any]
36	                 }] as [String: Any]
37	            }
38	        ]
39	    }
40	
41	    private static func view(_ view: UIView) -> [String: Any] {
42	        ["class": String(describing: type(of: view)),
43	         "id": view.accessibilityIdentifier ?? "",
44	         "frame": NSCoder.string(for: view.frame),
45	         "hidden": view.isHidden,
46	         "alpha": view.alpha,
47	         "background": view.backgroundColor?.description ?? "none",
48	         "subviewCount": view.subviews.count]
49	    }
50	
51	    private static func controller(_ controller: UIViewController, depth: Int = 0) -> [String: Any] {
52	        var result: [String: Any] = ["class": String(describing: type(of: controller)),
53	                                   "viewLoaded": controller.isViewLoaded]
54	        if let loadedView = controller.viewIfLoaded { result["view"] = view(loadedView) }
55	        guard depth < 8 else { return result }
56	        if let presented = controller.presentedViewController {
57	            result["presented"] = self.controller(presented, depth: depth + 1)
58	        }
59	        if let nav = controller as? UINavigationController {
60	            result["visibleController"] = nav.visibleViewController.map { String(describing: type(of: $0)) } ?? "none"
61	        }
62	        if let tab = controller as? UITabBarController { result["selectedTab"] = tab.selectedIndex }
63	        result["children"] = controller.children.map { self.controller($0, depth: depth + 1) }
64	        return result
65	    }
66	}

70	/// The published server theme (wac-v1) versus what this phone runs and what the build ships.
71	struct ThemeServerTool: NativeTool {
72	    let name = "theme_server"
73	    let description = """
74	    DEVELOPER. Inspect and manage the published app theme (wac-v1), which every phone runs in \
75	    preference to the theme shipped in the build. action=status: the running source, remote origin \
76	    and version, local override, sign-in, and hubRowShowsCard as running / shipped / server. \
77	    action=diff: every path where the server document differs from the shipped Theme.json (0 = in \
78	    lockstep; jobKindCatalogue is excluded — it has its own publication flow). \
79	    action=local_diff: this phone's UNPUBLISHED editor edits versus the server version they were \
80	    taken from — what the person changed locally, path by path. \
81	    action=discard_local: drop those local edits and run the server theme again. \
82	    action=publish_shipped (dry_run to preview): make the server theme EQUAL the build's shipped \
83	    Theme.json (jobKindCatalogue kept as on the server), schema-validated, conditional on the version \
84	    read — keeps source and online in lockstep; affects EVERY phone following wac-v1. \
85	    action=publish_setting (key, value_json; dry_run to preview): changes ONE top-level key of the \
86	    LIVE server document, keeping everything else, validated against WAC's schema, conditional on \
87	    the version read (a concurrent publish is refused), then adopted on this phone — affects EVERY \
88	    phone following wac-v1; signs in with the WAC login (a WAC App site designer) or the Ripul assistant. action=use_shipped: \
89	    this phone runs the shipped defaults (persists across relaunch; server untouched). \
90	    action=follow_server: back to the server theme, checking for a newer version.
91	    """
92	    let inputSchema = ToolSchema.object(
93	        .string("action", "status | diff | local_diff | discard_local | publish_setting | publish_shipped | use_shipped | follow_server; default status"),
94	        .string("key", "publish_setting: top-level theme key, e.g. hubRowShowsCard"),
95	        .string("value_json", "publish_setting: the new value as JSON, e.g. true, \"card\", {\"a\":1}"),
96	        .bool("dry_run", "publish_setting / publish_shipped: report the change without publishing (default false)")
97	    )
98	    let outputSchema: [String: Any]? = nil
99	    let timeout: TimeInterval = 30
100	
101	    @MainActor
102	    func execute(args: [String: Any]) async throws -> Any {
103	        switch args["action"] as? String ?? "status" {
104	        case "status":
105	            var result = ThemeProvider.themeDiagnostics
106	            result["serverStatus"] = await WACServerTheme.refreshStatus().summary
107	            return result
108	        case "diff":
109	            let diff = try await WACServerTheme.diffAgainstShipped()
110	            return ["serverVersion": diff.etag ?? "", "differences": diff.entries, "count": diff.entries.count] as [String: Any]
111	        case "publish_setting":
112	            guard let key = args["key"] as? String, !key.isEmpty else { throw ThemeToolError("publish_setting requires key") }
113	            guard let raw = args["value_json"] as? String,
114	                  let value = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(raw.utf8), options: [.fragmentsAllowed]) else {
115	                throw ThemeToolError("publish_setting requires value_json (valid JSON)")
116	            }
117	            if args["dry_run"] as? Bool == true {
118	                return try await WACServerTheme.previewChange(setting: key, to: value)
119	            }
120	            try await WACServerTheme.publish(setting: key, to: value)
121	            var result = ThemeProvider.themeDiagnostics
122	            result["published"] = ["key": key, "value": value]
123	            return result
124	        case "local_diff":
125	            return try WACServerTheme.localDiff()
126	        case "discard_local":
127	            ThemeProvider.resetToAuthoritativeTheme()
128	            var result = ThemeProvider.themeDiagnostics
129	            result["localEditsRemaining"] = try WACServerTheme.localDiff()["count"] ?? 0
130	            return result
131	        case "publish_shipped":
132	            if args["dry_run"] as? Bool == true {
133	                return try await WACServerTheme.previewShippedPublish()
134	            }
135	            try await WACServerTheme.publishShipped()
136	            let drift = try await WACServerTheme.diffAgainstShipped()
137	            var result = ThemeProvider.themeDiagnostics
138	            result["lockstepDifferences"] = drift.entries
139	            result["serverVersion"] = drift.etag ?? ""
140	            return result
141	        case "use_shipped":
142	            try ThemeProvider.useShippedTheme()
143	            return ThemeProvider.themeDiagnostics
144	        case "follow_server":
145	            ThemeProvider.resetToAuthoritativeTheme()
146	            return ThemeProvider.themeDiagnostics
147	        default:
148	            throw ThemeToolError("Unknown action")
149	        }
150	    }
151	}

15	 * A native API the web agent can call (twin of iOS `NativeTool`, NativeTool.swift).
16	 *
17	 * Naming, as on iOS: `pick_*` presents native UI and waits for a choice (return `name` or `value`
18	 * for the confirmation card), `get_*`/`list_*` read, `create_*`/`setup_*`/`delete_*` write.
19	 */
20	interface NativeTool {
21	    /** snake_case; the prefix drives the agent's behaviour (above). */
22	    val name: String
23	    val description: String
24	    /** JSON Schema of the input, built with [ToolSchema.obj]. */
25	    val inputSchema: JsonObject
26	    /** The fields the tool returns, shown to the agent as "Returns:" so it can chain `$ref` paths. */
27	    val outputSchema: JsonObject? get() = null
28	    /** Seconds before the web gives up; 0 waits indefinitely. */
29	    val timeoutSeconds: Double get() = 30.0
30	
31	    /** Runs the tool. Throw [ToolError] (or any exception) to answer the agent with its message. */
32	    suspend fun execute(args: JsonObject): JsonElement
33	
34	    /** The MCP definition sent to the web agent (`mcp:tools`); `timeout` in milliseconds for JS. */
35	    val definition: JsonObject get() = buildJsonObject {
36	        put("name", name)
37	        put("description", description)
38	        put("inputSchema", inputSchema)
39	        outputSchema?.let { put("outputSchema", it) }
40	        put("timeout", (timeoutSeconds * 1000).toLong())
41	    }
42	
43	    // Argument helpers, as iOS's.
44	
45	    /** A required string; throws [ToolError.InvalidArgs] when missing or not a string. */
46	    fun string(key: String, args: JsonObject): String =
47	        optionalString(key, args) ?: throw ToolError.InvalidArgs("Missing required string parameter '$key'")

package io.ripul.sdk.agent

import androidx.compose.foundation.isSystemInDarkTheme
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.rememberCoroutineScope
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.viewinterop.AndroidView

/** A bridge for the composition's lifetime, with [tools] registered. */
@Composable
fun rememberAgentBridge(vararg tools: NativeTool): AgentBridge {
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    return remember(scope) { AgentBridge(scope).also { b -> tools.forEach(b::register) } }
}

/**
 * The web agent as a Compose view (twin of iOS `AgentView`): the agent page in [AgentWebView],
 * talking to [bridge], whose native tools the agent can call.
 */
@Composable
fun AgentView(
    configuration: AgentConfiguration,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    bridge: AgentBridge = rememberAgentBridge(),
) {
    val dark = isSystemInDarkTheme()
    AndroidView(
        factory = { context -> AgentWebView(context, configuration, bridge, dark).also { it.loadAgent() } },
        modifier = modifier,
        onRelease = { it.destroy() },
    )
}

# Ripul Android SDK

The Android twin of `ripul-ios-sdk`: a CMS site drawn natively with Jetpack
Compose and Material 3, plus the SDK-host core an app needs. The plan, the
iOS → Android file map, the conventions and each area's status are in
[docs/plans/ripul-android-sdk.md](../docs/plans/ripul-android-sdk.md).

## Build and test

```bash
cd ripul-android-sdk
./gradlew :ripul:testDebugUnitTest                 # JVM tests, including the shared case tables
./gradlew :examples:wac-next:assembleDebug         # WAC Next (com.wac.next) → wac-app
./gradlew :examples:control-playground:assembleDebug
```

JDK 17 and the Android SDK come from the shell: agents' shells on the Studio
already have `JAVA_HOME` (`~/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/temurin-17.jdk`)
and `ANDROID_HOME` (`~/Library/Android/sdk`). Keep that one JDK in every
checkout: builds share their Gradle and Kotlin daemons only when the JDK and
`gradle.properties` match. `local.properties` (gitignored) is optional, with
`sdk.dir=$HOME/Library/Android/sdk`.

Several agents build at once, each in its own worktree. `gradle.properties`
keeps their memory down: one shared Kotlin daemon, a 3 GB Gradle heap, and
daemons that exit after 15 idle minutes.

Emulators are borrowed through Trainyard (`ripul-train acquire android …`).

# Sharing a device with someone else's chat

A person using an app built with the SDK can let the agent in another
person's Ripul chat read the app on their phone: a designer's unpublished
theme draft, say, read by a developer's agent. Nothing is shared until they
say so, only tools that read are shared, and it stops when they press Stop,
when they close the app, or after an hour.

Built 10 November 2026. The whole flow, the server's rules and the tests are
in `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/memberDevices.md`.

## What the app does: say which tools only read

A tool is shared only when it says it changes nothing:

```swift
struct ThemeServerTool: NativeTool {
    let name = "theme_server"
    let access: NativeToolAccess = .reads      // the app's own data
    …
}

public struct InspectScreenTool: NativeTool {
    public let access: NativeToolAccess = .readsScreen   // what is on screen
    …
}
```

- `.changes` is the default. A tool that says nothing is never shared.
- `.reads`: reads the app's own data and changes nothing, not even a local
  draft, a setting or a cache.
- `.readsScreen`: reads what is on screen. Shared only when the person also
  chose to share their screen.

One action that changes anything makes the whole tool `.changes`. Split a tool
whose actions mix reading and changing: wac's `theme_server` became
`theme_server` (status, diff, local_diff) and `theme_server_edit` (the actions
that delete the phone's draft or publish).

The SDK's own tools that read the screen say so: `inspect_screen`,
`screen_frame`, `screen_audit`, `wait_for_element`. So do `get_theme_style`
and `list_theme_scopes`. Console and network logs do not, because they can
carry credentials.

On Android the same field is `NativeTool.access`, with `NativeToolAccess.READS`
and `READS_SCREEN`.

## What the person sees

- **A card in the chat**, put there when the chat owner's agent asks for their
  device: share the app's tools that read, those and the screen, or not now.
  The app it is answered in is the one shared, so the card says to answer it
  in that app. In an app without what the agent asked for, answering is
  refused.
- **A pill at the top of the screen** while it is shared: "“Wac theme” can read
  this app", with Stop. It is Live View's pill (`LiveStreamIndicator`) with its
  own words, shrinks to a "Shared" mark after a few seconds and opens again
  each time the chat reads something. `DeviceSharingIndicator.swift` shows it,
  from the page's `agent-framework:device:sharing` reports; Stop calls the
  page's `window.__ripulStopDeviceSharing()`.
- On Android, `AgentBridge.deviceShares` and `stopDeviceSharing()`, and
  `DeviceSharingBanner(bridge)` for the app to place at the top of its screens.

The page tells the app nothing else, and keeps the person's choice itself
(`relay/memberDevice.ts`). The page also learns the app's name at start
(`window.__ripulHostAppName`, from `CFBundleDisplayName`), so the chat sees
"wac on iPhone".

## Store builds

Sharing is public API only. What can be shared is what the build compiles in:
wac's developer tools, `theme_server` among them, are in developer builds
only. Customers of an App Store build are reached through support sessions
(`support-sessions.md`); reading tools over a support session are not built
yet.

## Limits

- The app must be open, and the chat connected: an iPhone app in the
  background answers nothing.
- One hour at a time. The person shares again for more.
- Only the chat owner's own turns can use it.
