# A member's device, shared with a chat for reading

Someone invited to a chat can let that chat's agent read the app on their
own device: wac's `theme_server local_diff` on a designer's iPhone, read by
the owner's agent to see the designer's unpublished theme. Built 10
November 2026 (Peter's decisions that day: in store builds too, only while
the app is open, the screen as its own consent, only the owner's turns).

A member's device is never in the owner's machine room, and since 31 October
2026 a device takes no device commands from a Mac on another account
(`sharedMacAccess.md`, "A member's own devices are not the Mac's"). That stays.
This is the one way an agent reaches a member's device, through the chat's
own channel, the way a member's browser is reached (`mcpToolSurfaces.md`, "A
member's own browser").

## How it goes

1. The owner's agent calls a device tool naming a member:
   `device_theme_server` with `device: "member-x7k2qp"`. `device_list_targets`
   lists the chat's members who could share (`members.membersWhoCanShare`) and
   the devices shared now (`members.sharedWithThisChat`).
2. Not shared yet: nothing runs. The host puts a card in the chat for that
   member (`relay/memberDevicePrompt.ts`): share the app's tools that read,
   those and the screen, or not now. The card names what the agent wants.
3. The member answers on the device to be shared. Only the person the card
   names may answer (`member_device_share_<userId>_<uuid>`), and the answer
   never travels: `submitToolResult` hands it to `answerDeviceShareCard`, which
   refuses in an app that has none of the tools the card asked for (answered
   in the Ripul app on the same phone, the Ripul app would be the one shared).
4. That device keeps the choice (`ripul.memberDevice.shared.v1`, per chat, an
   hour), holds the chat's socket open with the member's invitation, and offers
   its tools that say they only read (`session.deviceOffer`). The SDK draws a
   pill with Stop.
5. The server keeps the offer on that socket (`sessionChannel/memberDevice.ts`)
   and tells the owner's connections (`session.devicePeers`). The host's card
   closes and the chat carries on by itself, still the owner's turn
   (`resumeChat`, sent as `RESUME_SENDER`).
6. The agent calls again with the device's handle,
   `device: "member-x7k2qp-iphone"`. The host sends `session.deviceQuery`; the
   server passes it only to the device named, only for a tool in its offer;
   the device checks its own record and its own tools again, runs the tool, and
   the answer comes back stamped with the member's identity by the server.

## What holds

| Where | Check |
|---|---|
| The tool (SDK) | `NativeTool.access`: `.reads`, `.readsScreen` or the default `.changes` (`ripul-ios-sdk/docs/sharing-a-device.md`) |
| The member's device (`relay/memberDevice.ts`) | Shares nothing until the member answers; offers only `reads` tools, and `screen` ones only if chosen; refuses any request for a tool it does not share, whatever the server passed; ends at Stop, at its hour, or when the server says it has ended |
| The server (`sessionChannel/memberDevice.ts`) | Takes an offer only from a named invitee or a teammate in a team chat; refuses a whole offer that names any tool not saying it only reads; holds a share to an hour; takes a query only from the owner's own connection, only for a tool in the offer, only to the member named; a result only from the device asked |
| The owner's host (`frame-bridge/memberDeviceRoute.ts`) | A member's device is reached only by naming it, never as a default; only in the owner's own turns (`invitedRequesterFor` and `teamRequesterFor` are empty); a tool not shared is refused before anything is sent |

A member's device is never the working device, takes no lease and is never
in Trainyard. Every call is a tool row in the chat, which the member sees, and
each result says where it ran (`_device`, `_deviceLabel`, `_notice`).

## Handles

`member-<6 of the user id>-<platform>`: `member-x7k2qp-iphone`. The member's
own handle (`member-x7k2qp`, the same as their browser's) reaches their one
shared device, or asks them when they share none. Two devices of one platform
take the end of their socket id: `member-x7k2qp-iphone-1a2b`. A member's socket
gets a new id each time it connects, so handles are built from the member and
the platform, not the socket.

## Limits

- The app must be open and its chat connected: in the background it answers
  nothing.
- An hour at a time.
- Reading only. Nothing that taps, types or changes the device can be shared.
- Customers of an App Store build have no Ripul account and are not chat
  members. They are reached through support sessions
  (`ripul-ios-sdk/docs/support-sessions.md`), where tool calls are not built
  yet.
- Android: the tool field, the sharing state and a banner composable exist;
  Android's SDK has no chat screen of its own, so its app needs one to answer
  the card.

## Tests

```bash
cd chrome-extension
npx vitest run src/relay/memberDevice.test.ts src/frame-bridge/memberDeviceRoute.test.ts
cd packages/api && npx vitest run src/sessionChannel/memberDevice.test.ts src/sessionChannel/__tests__/memberDevice.test.ts
cd ripul-android-sdk && ./gradlew :ripul:testDebugUnitTest --tests 'io.ripul.sdk.agent.AgentBridgeTest'
```

{"guide":"# Trains: builds and deploys shared between agents

When several agents work on one Mac, their builds and deploys collide: two deploys overwrite each other, a rebuild restarts an app someone is testing, an install lands on a phone mid-test. Trainyard, part of Ripul Host, queues that work. A **track** is one job (a deploy, a build, an install). Agents ask for it; one run serves everyone waiting.

## What works in any repository

Holds, held-back commits and borrowing a simulator need no setup:

```bash
ripul-train status     # what is running, queued, held and held back here, and whether this repository has tracks
ripul-train hold <resource> --reason "…" --ttl 20
ripul-train acquire simulators os=27 type=iPhone --reason "…" --wait   # see the devices guide
```

**Tracks** (shared builds and deploys) are defined per repository, in `.ripul/trains.yaml`. Where a repository has them, use them, and do not run the underlying build or deploy command yourself, even if you can see it in the file. `ripul-train config` lists them, or says the repository has none.

## Build slots

Each Mac runs only a few builds at once. Your `xcodebuild` (and `xcrun xcodebuild`) takes one of its build slots, in any repository, with nothing to set up; a question to Xcode (`-list`, `-version`, `-showBuildSettings`) does not. Build as the repository's instructions say: the slots apply to that command as it is.

- **When every slot is in use, the build waits and says so** on stderr: `Ripul: waiting for a build slot (2 of 2 in use: …). Place 1 in the queue.` That is working as intended. It then runs and exits with the build's own status.
- **Do not stop a waiting build to try again or to build some other way.** If your command has a time limit, run the build detached (`nohup … > build.log 2>&1 &`) and read its log. A command that is stopped while waiting keeps its place for 90 seconds: running the same command again from the same folder takes it up.
- **Two builds cannot share one `-derivedDataPath`** at once; the second waits for the first. Reuse a folder an earlier build of this checkout used: a new one compiles everything from scratch, and the wrapper says so.
- `ripul-train builds` shows the slots, who holds them, who is waiting, and the last builds. Turning the slots off (`ripul-train builds off`) is a person's call.

## Using a track

```bash
ripul-train request <track> --wait          # board the train and wait for the result
ripul-train hold <resource> --reason "testing sign-in" --ttl 20
ripul-train release <hold-id>               # as soon as the test is done
ripul-train block <commit> --reason "not to ship until the owner says"
ripul-train unblock <block-id>
```

- **Check where the track builds.** Normally it builds the remote branch in a clean worktree: commit and push first. A track configured with `worktree: false` builds the requesting checkout in place, subject to its clean-path checks; it can use committed work that has not been pushed. Read `ripul-train config` before assuming which source it uses.
- **Take a hold before a test that depends on a shared thing** (the live build, a phone, a running app), and release it straight after. A hold keeps trains that would disturb that thing in the yard. Holds expire: 15 minutes by default, 60 at most.
- **A block stops the whole train**, including other agents' work queued behind that commit. It is for "this must not go live yet", not for routine caution.
- **A finished job and a host reload are separate.** `--wait` returns when the train finishes its job. A reload or restart configured with `when-idle` can still be due; read the arrival status before claiming the running host has the new code.
- A repository's own scripts may board a train for you. Its instructions file will say which.

## Arrivals and notifications

`ripul-train status` lists due reloads or restarts separately from shipped trains. A due step waits for idle agents and holds on its resource; a later train can join the same step so one reload serves both. A failed arrival does not undo the shipped build. Verify the running app's build when that is what your test depends on.

`ripul-train force <due-id>` runs an arrival over busy agents, but not over a hold; it can interrupt their work. `ripul-train cancel <due-id>` drops it. Use these only when the requested work authorizes that disruption; do not force a reload just to finish waiting.

A train requested without `--wait` notifies its requesting chat when it ends and starts another turn. A chat busy with other work then is told when that turn ends; one whose turn is watching the train with `--wait` is not told again. A host restart that must wait for the requester delays its notification until that arrival ends. `ripul-train notices` shows delivery, and `ripul-train notices off` disables notices.","next":"For another task, request this topic without section to see its section directory.","section":"deploy","title":"Use an existing track","topic":"trains"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# release-public.sh — Publish the monorepo RipulAgent SDK to the public
# ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk repo as a clean, one-way mirror + version tag.
#
# The monorepo copy (this script's parent dir) is the source of truth. Histories
# between the two repos diverged long ago, so we do NOT merge — we overwrite the
# public repo's working tree with the monorepo SDK (rsync --delete), commit, and
# tag vX.Y.Z. The push to GitHub happens ONLY with --push (outward-facing step).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/release-public.sh 0.1.0           # stage locally (mirror + commit + tag), no push
#   scripts/release-public.sh 0.1.0 --push    # also push commit + tag to origin
#
# Env:
#   RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK   path to the public repo clone
#                      (default: $HOME/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk)
set -euo pipefail

VERSION="${1:-}"
PUSH=""
[ "${2:-}" = "--push" ] && PUSH=1

SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"          # monorepo SDK root
DEST="${RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK:-$HOME/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk}"        # public repo clone
REMOTE_NAME="origin"
TAG="v${VERSION}"

die() { echo "❌ $*" >&2; exit 1; }

62:  git -C "$SRC" commit -q -m "chore(sdk): stamp ripulSDKVersion $VERSION"

description: "WAC iOS default build target = device-first then prod OTA, no asking; scripts/ship-wac.sh encodes it. Recurring footgun: never bare -scheme WAC (drops Pods -> Alamofire fail)"
metadata:

Peter was frustrated we "rediscover all the footguns every time" and re-run/re-build. Standing policy for getting a WAC build onto a device — **do not ask which target, just do it in this order**:

1. Peter's iPhone 17 Pro Max (UDID `00008150-001C544E0EBA401C`) reachable → fast incremental **build + install to phone**.
2. Otherwise → fast incremental **prod OTA**.

**Just run `nohup bash scripts/ship-wac.sh > /tmp/wac-ship.log 2>&1 &`** (device-first, else prod OTA, no prompt). Overrides: `WAC_TARGET=device|ota`, `WAC_NOTES="..."`, `scripts/ship-wac.sh <udid>`. Launch DETACHED — session recycles mid-build.

**Why:** stop re-deciding the target and stop hand-rolling `xcodebuild`. Footguns that cost real build cycles this session (all avoided by the committed scripts):
- **Never bare `-scheme WAC`; always `-workspace WAC.xcworkspace`.** Bare builds the `.xcodeproj`, omits CocoaPods → `Unable to find module dependency: 'Alamofire'` in `RotaCardWidgetExtension`. Looks like a code error; it's the wrong project.
- **Reuse a warm `-derivedDataPath`** (`/tmp/wac-device-dd`). Cold dir = unresolved SPM + full rebuild.
- **macOS eats `/tmp` files unopened for 3 days.** After a few idle days the dd's `SourcePackages/checkouts/*` keep their folders but lose files, and the build dies at once with `Could not resolve package dependencies: the package manifest at '…/checkouts/<pkg>/Package.swift' cannot be accessed`. No
- Prod = `WAC` scheme / **Release** config (Debug maps to Dev.xcconfig = dev backend, breaks login). FAST=1 incremental ~1-2 min, not the old 5-10 min archive.

**How to apply:** for any "build/ship/deploy to my phone / get it on device" ask in WAC, run `ship-wac.sh` detached without asking. content.content:
**Production** (prod backend) and **Dev / Test** sections. Each "Install" button is an
  `itms-services://?action=download-manifest&url=…/manifest-<…>.plist` link.
- **`manifest-<flavor>-<B>.plist`** — standard itms-services manifest pointing at the IPA;
  `bundle-identifier` = the flavour's own id (see below), `bundle-version = <B>`.
- **`WAC-<flavor>-<B>.ipa`** — the app, **development-signed** (Apple Development, team
  `C7AA358R56`). The installing device **must be in the provisioning profile**, and the
  user must trust the developer afterwards (Settings → General → VPN & Device Management).
- **Build number `<B>`** = `YYYYMMDDHHMM` timestamp.
- **Each flavour has its OWN bundle id** via `com.WAC$(BUNDLE_ID_SUFFIX)` (prod `com.WAC`,
  beta `com.WAC.beta`, staging `com.WAC.staging`, dev `com.WAC.dev`, business
  `com.WAC.business`) — flavours install **alongside** each other, never replacing.
  ("WAC Beta" therefore means the `com.WAC.beta` app — a production-backend test app —
  NOT a TestFlight/pre-release of the prod app; see CLAUDE.md "'WAC beta' is a FLAVOR".)

### Flavours

| Flavour | Scheme | Archive config | Backend | `isTestingBuild` (debug screens) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **dev** | `WAC(Dev)` | `Release(Dev)` | `app.workandcommunications.co.uk:3000` | **yes** — Debug hub visible |
| **staging** | `WAC(Staging)` | `Release(Staging)` | prod (`api3…`) | **yes** — Debug hub visible |
| **prod** | `WAC` | `Release` | prod (`api3…`) | **no** — Debug hub hidden |

`isTestingBuild` is `AppleAppID != 1483618032` (the prod App Store id), set per-xcconfig in
`WAC/Configuration/{Dev,Staging,Production}.xcconfig`. So **the dev-only Debug screens only
ship in dev/staging builds, never prod.**

---

## Prerequisites

- Signing for team `C7AA358R56`: either the team's App Store Connect key in
  `~/.ripul/appstoreconnect/key.json` (the scripts pass it through `scripts/asc-key.sh`,
  and nobody need be signed in to Xcode), or Xcode signed in to the team. Target device
  registered in the profile. The key is explained in the Ripul repo's
  `ripul-native-app/docs/app-store-connect-api-key.md`.
- `node`/`npx` (for `wrangler`).
- **`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`** exported (R2 read/write to the `wac-ota` bucket).
- The bucket is on Cloudflare account **`48994301be053cfc75d066dfaed15e35`**; the script pins
  `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` to it (see gotcha 2).

---

## Deploy
Reach for the OTA script directly only when you specifically want dev/staging/beta, or a
build number shared across flavours.

### OTA directly (dev/staging/prod)

`deploy-wac-ota.sh` defaults to **`FAST=1`** — reuse the warm `/tmp/wac-device-dd` cache and
do a plain incremental `build` (no full archive), then package that `.app` as the IPA. On a
repeat build that's **~1–2 min**. Set `FAST=0` for a clean, fully-optimised archive.

> **Always run detached with `nohup … &`.** Even the fast path is multi-minute. Claude's
> background shell runner is a child process — when the session is torn down (context
> compaction, app restart, timeout) the OS SIGHUPs and kills all children. `nohup` makes the
> build survive; `&` detaches it. Without it, the build is silently killed mid-build.

```bash
# one build number shared across both flavours in this deploy
```

input.title: SDK's MainThreadSampler breaks x86_64 simulator builds
input.detail:
`ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/MainThreadSampler.swift:211-215` uses `arm_thread_state64_t` and `ARM_THREAD_STATE64` with no `#if arch(arm64)` guard. Any build that compiles the x86_64 simulator slice fails, for example wac's compile check with `-destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator"` on SDK 0.7.183 (10 Nov 2026):

```
MainThreadSampler.swift:211:21: error: cannot find 'arm_thread_state64_t' in scope
```

Device builds (arm64) and Apple Silicon simulators building only their own architecture are unaffected. Fix: put the ARM thread-state read inside `#if arch(arm64)`, with an empty stand-in otherwise, then release the SDK. Until then, consumers' generic simulator builds need `ARCHS=arm64`.
